types.name: Personal Area Network
types.desc: Connects devices centered on a single person's workspace.

types.name: Local Area Network
types.range: Within a room, building, or office campus (up to 1 km)
types.desc: High data transfer rate, low error rate, privately owned.

types.name: Campus Area Network
types.range: 1 km to 5 km (university or military base)
types.desc: Spans multiple contiguous buildings belonging to one organization.

types.name: Metropolitan Area Network
types.range: 5 km to 50 km (entire city or large metro area)
types.tech: Cable TV network, WiMAX, city fiber loops
types.desc: Spans a city; larger than LAN, smaller than WAN.

types.name: Wide Area Network
types.tech: Leased lines, satellite links, underwater fiber cables
types.desc: The Internet is the world's largest public WAN. High latency compared to LAN.

types.name: Storage Area Network
types.desc: Dedicated high-speed network that interconnects and delivers shared pools of storage devices.

types.name: Virtual Private Network
types.desc: Creates a secure, encrypted tunnel across a public network like the Internet.

topologies.name: Star Topology
topologies.structure: All devices connected to a central Hub or Switch.
topologies.advantages: Easy to install and wire; failure of one cable/device only disconnects that device, central monitoring.
topologies.disadvantages: Central hub/switch is a Single Point of Failure (if central hub fails, whole network goes down).
topologies.cablesNeeded: N cables (where N is number of nodes)
topologies.examFrequency: Most widely used topology in modern LANs.

topologies.name: Mesh Topology
topologies.structure: Every device is connected to every other device via dedicated point-to-point links (Fully Connected Mesh).
topologies.advantages: Highest fault tolerance, robust, dedicated traffic with no congestion, maximum privacy.
topologies.disadvantages: Most expensive, massive cabling, difficult installation and maintenance.
topologies.formula: Number of duplex links = N * (N - 1) / 2 | Number of I/O ports per device = N - 1
topologies.examFrequency: Extremely frequent math calculation in bank exams! (e.g., 6 devices require 6*5/2 = 15 cables).

topologies.name: Bus Topology
topologies.structure: All devices share a single common communication line called a 'Backbone' cable, terminated at both ends with Terminators.
topologies.advantages: Minimal cabling required, cost-effective for small networks.
topologies.disadvantages: If backbone cable breaks anywhere, entire network goes down. Difficult troubleshooting, packet collisions (uses CSMA/CD).
topologies.terminatorRole: Absorbs signals to prevent signal reflection (echo) which causes line noise.

topologies.name: Ring Topology
topologies.structure: Devices connected in a circular closed loop. Data travels in one direction (unidirectional) or bidirectional (dual ring).
topologies.advantages: Predictable transmission via Token Passing (Token Ring - IEEE 802.5), no collisions.
topologies.disadvantages: Break in the ring breaks the entire network unless using a redundant dual ring (FDDI).

topologies.name: Tree Topology
topologies.structure: Hierarchical combination of Star and Bus topologies. Root node connects to secondary hubs.
topologies.advantages: Highly scalable, easy expansion of corporate branch networks.
topologies.disadvantages: Failure of root trunk cable disables the dependent branches.

topologies.name: Hybrid Topology
topologies.structure: Combination of two or more different topologies (e.g., Star-Ring, Star-Bus).

devices.name: Repeater
devices.desc: Regenerates and amplifies attenuated signals over long cable runs. Operates on raw bits, does not read headers.

devices.name: Hub
devices.desc: Multi-port repeater. Broadcasts all incoming packets to ALL connected ports (dumb device). High collisions, single collision domain, single broadcast domain.

devices.name: Bridge
devices.desc: Connects two LAN segments using the same protocol. Filters traffic based on MAC addresses. Divides network into 2 collision domains.

devices.name: Switch
devices.desc: Intelligent multi-port bridge. Builds a MAC Address Table (CAM Table) through learning. Forwards frames only to destination port (unicast). Each port is its own separate collision domain.

devices.name: Router
devices.desc: Connects disparate networks (e.g. LAN to WAN / Internet). Routes packets based on logical IP addresses using routing protocols (OSPF, BGP). Blocks broadcasts (breaks broadcast domains).

devices.name: Gateway
devices.desc: Protocol translator / converter. Connects two completely different network architectures (e.g., AppleTalk to TCP/IP, or legacy mainframe to cloud).

devices.name: Modem (Modulator-Demodulator)
devices.desc: Converts digital data from computer into analog signals for telephone/cable lines, and vice versa.

collisionVsBroadcastDomain.collisionDomain: Network segment where packet collisions can occur if two devices transmit simultaneously. Hub = 1 collision domain for all ports. Switch = Each port is a separate collision domain.
collisionVsBroadcastDomain.broadcastDomain: Portion of network where any device sending a broadcast frame will be received by all other devices. Hub and Switch maintain 1 broadcast domain. Router breaks broadcast domains.

guided.name: Twisted Pair Cable
guided.categories: Cat 5e (1 Gbps up to 100m), Cat 6 (10 Gbps up to 55m), Cat 6a (10 Gbps up to 100m)
guided.desc: Pairs of wires twisted together to cancel electromagnetic interference (EMI) and crosstalk.

guided.name: Coaxial Cable
guided.desc: Central copper conductor surrounded by dielectric insulator, metallic braided shield, and plastic jacket.

guided.name: Fiber Optic Cable
guided.types: Single-Mode (long distance, laser, thin core 9µm) vs Multi-Mode (short distance, LED, thicker core 50-62.5µm)
guided.desc: Transmits light pulses through glass/plastic core. Immune to EMI and radio interference, highest bandwidth.

unguided.name: Radio Waves
unguided.propagation: Omnidirectional (travels in all directions). Penetrates building walls. Used in AM/FM radio, Wi-Fi, cellular.

unguided.name: Microwaves
unguided.propagation: Line-of-Sight (unidirectional, narrow focused beam). Blocked by obstacles. Used in satellite and radar communication.

unguided.name: Infrared Waves
unguided.propagation: Line-of-Sight, short range. Cannot penetrate walls (high security). Used in TV remote controls.
